newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo shares plunge, Hong Kong hits fresh high.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo shares plunge, Hong Kong hits fresh high.

text.p: Japanese stocks lost over 600 points on Monday after a policy speech by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto failed to soothe nervous investors, while markets in Hong Kong, Australia, New Zealand and Taiwan hit fresh highs.
The key Nikkei stock index closed sharply lower, reflecting disappointment with a speech to parliament in which Hashimoto vowed to press ahead with tax rises and repeated pledges of broad reforms.

The market's key barometer, the Nikkei 225 average, closed down 609.70 points, or 3.37 percent, at 17,480.34. It had briefly dived around 850 points to 17,237.27 ahead of the speech as the market guessed accurately that Hashimoto would have little new to say to bolster confidence in the stock market.
The Nikkei plunged over 2,000 points in the first trading week of 1997 on worries that the government's forthcoming tax increases could derail Japan's fragile economic recovery.
Elsewhere in Asia, markets were buoyant after Wall Street's 68-point, or one percent, leap on Friday to a new record high.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index edged to its fourth straight record close, led by lagging conglomerates, but the index ended off the day's highs as other stocks suffered profit-taking and Japanese shares fell.
The Hang Seng rose 11.84 points, or 0.09 percent, to 13,868.24 after hitting a session high of 13,994.86.

"People were buying laggards," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities. "In this recent rally we saw banks rally and property stocks rise but the conglomerates have not done anything," he said.
In Australia, strength on Wall Street, combined with hopes of a further local interest rate cut, boosted the Australian share market to a record close.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished 8.7 points firmer at 2,444.2, eclipsing its previous record close of 2,348.2 which was set on January 15.

New Zealand's top 40 share index ended within striking distance of a three-year high. The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 10.65 points stronger at 2,440.21, its highest level since reaching 2,444.80 in early February, 1994.
In Taiwan, share prices surged 1.40 percent to notch their highest close since June 1990 on hopes of a renewed rally around the February 7 Chinese lunar new year, brokers said.
The weighted TAIEX index gained 100.12 points to 7,254.32, surpassing the 7,206.42 point close of January 16, which until Monday was the highest level since 7,339.71 on June 5, 1990.

The Jakarta Composite Index surged to a new high, up 10.16 points, or 1.53 percent, to 674.13 points. Brokers said the index was at its highest level since April 1990, when it hit a record 681.94 points.

South Korean stocks closed sharply higher on hopes of a political solution to labour unrest after President Kim Young-sam's proposal to discuss the crisis with opposition leaders on Tuesday. The composite stock index closed up 24.23 points or 3.49 percent at 718.46.

Singapore's stock market had one of its busiest days in months as foreign funds led a bargain-hunt for cheap local blue chip stocks. The benchmark 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index closed 27.67 points higher at 2,271.88.
Stocks in Thailand closed 1.02 percent higher as speculators bought stocks ahead of the release of fourth quarter earnings results of finance firms from Tuesday, brokers said.
The SET index rose for the second consecutive trading day, advancing 8.48 points to 841.03.

Manila shares finished lower as most blue chips tumbled and punters started taking profits on speculative issues, traders said. The bourse's benchmark index dipped 13.46 pts, or 0.41 pct, closing at 3,280.85.
Bombay shares retreated as a lack of follow-up buying from foreign funds prompted speculators to unwind positions in pivotal stocks, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 36.46 points, or 1.07 percent lower at 3,385.89, off 3,478.0, the intra-day high.

Crude oil futures weakened in Singapore, continuing to test lower prices after a bearish tone last week. March Brent was last traded at $22.40/$22.55 per barrel after London shed 53 cents down at $22.54.
Hong Kong gold ended at US$354.90/355.40 an ounce against New York's $355.30/80 close on Friday.

The dollar hit a new 31-month high of 1.4115 against the Swiss franc and was off earlier highs but testing key resistance levels against the mark and the yen in Europe. At 1015 GMT, the dollar was at 117.70/7.80 yen and 1.6220/30 marks.
